requirements:
This model represents some entities of a course. 
We know that courses have a name and a specific number of credits. Each course can have one or more professors, who have a name.
Professors could participate in any number of courses. For a course to exist, it must aggregate, at least, five students, where each student has a name. Students can be enrolled in any number of courses. Finally, students can be accommodated in dormitories, where each dormitory can have from one to four students. Besides, each dormitory has a price.

issues.message: Redundant and conflicting relationships between Course and Student.
issues.evidence: For a course to exist, it must aggregate, at least, five students... Students can be enrolled in any number of courses.
suggestions: Remove the separate association between Student and Course. The aggregation relationship already covers the enrollment requirement. If a separate association is needed for enrollment, the aggregation should be removed to avoid redundancy.

issues.message: Incorrect multiplicity on the Professor-Course relationship.
issues.evidence: Each course can have one or more professors... Professors could participate in any number of courses.
suggestions: Change the multiplicity on the Professor side to '*' and the Course side to '1..*'. The current model implies a professor must be associated with at least one course to exist, which is not stated.
